newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes higher on fund buying, quiet day.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes higher on fund buying, quiet day.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed higher early on fund buying but the demand was not aggressive and volume was thin, traders said.
"There wasn't anything to move the market and probably won't be until next week or next year," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.
Traders said end of the year profit taking and short covering was featured, they said.
Funds have been short the markets, especially the corn market, and were getting out of some of those positions before the year's end, the traders said.
Fundamentals were little changed, they said.
Only routine exports of U.S. wheat and overall good conditions in the U.S. winter wheat growing region continued to cap rallies, they said.
Merrill Lynch Futures and Refco Inc each bought 1.5 million bushels of March, the traders said.
Wheat futures closed one to three cents per bushel higher, with March up 2-1/4 at $3.94.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 9,000 contracts, more than the 4,567 traded Tuesday, according to the CBOT.
In wheat options, Term Commodities, the marketing arm of Louis Dreyfus Corp, sold 150 March $3.90 calls at 16-1/2 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 2,000 contracts compared with the 644 traded Tuesday.
